name: write_unaligned
declaration: const unsafe fn write_unaligned (self , val : T) where T : Sized ,
documentation:
Overwrites a memory location with the given value without reading or
 dropping the old value.

 Unlike `write`, the pointer may be unaligned.

 See [`ptr::write_unaligned`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::write_unaligned`]: crate::ptr::write_unaligned()
rules: For safety, self must be valid for writes of a value of type T.
The pointer in self need not be aligned for T.
It is safe for this call to overwrite the old contents of self without dropping them, even if doing so leaks allocations or resources.

When constructing the pointer wrapped by self to an unaligned packed struct field, no intermediate unaligned reference may be created, even temporarily before an immediate cast to a raw pointer; use &raw mut instead of forming such a reference.
